# Dock preview overlay renders in the host's flow unless the consumer positions it

## Context

Measured on 2026-09-02 in a downstream dock workspace app (engine checkout at `dev@ec6856b804`, Chrome): after a pane was pinned to its right-edge rail and pinned back, the whole workspace stood exactly one host width to the LEFT of the viewport — an empty dock under the app's menu bar. Switching tabs in a two-tab container did the same. Neither reproduced in `apps/workstation`.

The difference is one stylesheet rule the Workstation carries and the downstream host did not:

```scss
// resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss:259
> .neo-dock-preview { inset: 0; pointer-events: none; position: absolute; z-index: 25; }
```

The engine's own sheet never positions the preview's ROOT. `resources/scss/src/dashboard/dock/interaction/Preview.scss:7` gives `.neo-dock-preview` only `pointer-events: none`; `position: absolute` appears on the affordances INSIDE it (`:15`) and on the dwell pseudo-element (`:41`). The sibling overlay does position itself: `.neo-dashboard-dock-drop-indicators { inset: 0; position: absolute; z-index: 30 }` (`resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss:601`). Every consumer so far re-derived the missing pair for the preview: the Demo-A example (`resources/scss/src/examples/dashboard/choreography/DemoAWorkspace.scss:79`), the Workstation (added after the July 2026 finding that its overlays were drawn a header height too high), and now the downstream workspace, whose host had copied the Workstation's `position: relative` and stopped there.

## The Problem

A dock host lays out `fit`, i.e. a flex row. An unpositioned preview is an in-flow `neo-layout-fit-item` there — `flex: 1 0 100%`, as wide as the host — so the host's content is twice its width. `overflow-x: hidden` hides the scrollbar but the host stays programmatically scrollable, and any focus or scroll-into-view aimed at content right of the first width scrolls it:

| moment | host `clientWidth` | `scrollWidth` | `scrollLeft` | first shell x |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| boot, preview in flow | 1600 | 3200 | 0 | 0 |
| pin-back clicked while the reveal was still sliding in | 1600 | 3200 | 1561 | -1561 |
| tab switch in a two-tab container | 1600 | 3200 | 1423 | -1423 |
| same cycles with the preview positioned absolutely | 1600 | 1600 | 0 | 0 |

Nothing scrolls the host back: the preview keeps the overflow alive after the re-projection has retired the old shell, so the shift is permanent until a reload. With the preview lifted out of the flow the host has no overflow, a scroll during the staged swap (two shells, twice the width, for a few frames) clamps back to 0 the moment the old shell goes, and the recorded pin cycle shows zero `scroll` events.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` hosts the projection at `dockShellIndex` and keeps the preview and the indicator layer as persistent SIBLINGS in the same host (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`, `dockHostReference` / `dockShellIndex`); `DragAffordances` positions the preview's affordances in host-local coordinates (`localRect`) — the contract assumes the preview's box IS the host's box.
- `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` stages the next shell as a hidden sibling at `shellIndex + 1` (`src/dashboard/dock/projection/Reconciler.mjs:426`) — for the duration of the transaction the host legitimately holds two full-width shells, so the host MUST be able to recover from a transient scroll; it can only do that when nothing else keeps it scrollable.
- The indicator layer already owns its positioning in the engine sheet; the preview is the one overlay whose geometry a consumer has to know about.

## The Fix

1. `resources/scss/src/dashboard/dock/interaction/Preview.scss`: position the root — `.neo-dock-preview { inset: 0; pointer-events: none; position: absolute; }` — with a stacking value that keeps it under the indicator layer (`z-index: 30`) and above the reveal overlay (`z-index: 20`), i.e. the `25` the Workstation and Demo-A declare today (consumers may keep overriding `z-index`).
2. Retire the now-redundant consumer duplicates in `apps/workstation/Workspace.scss:259` and `DemoAWorkspace.scss:79`, or leave them as documented no-ops — one owner for the rule either way.
3. A geometry witness: the dock host's `scrollWidth` equals its `clientWidth` with nothing but `position: relative` on the host, asserted where the overlays are already measured (`test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationDragAffordancesNL.spec.mjs` or a component spec on a bare `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` with `dockHostReference`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.neo-dock-preview` is absolutely positioned with `inset: 0` by the engine sheet; a consumer host that declares only `position: relative` renders the preview over the host, not beside the shell.
- [ ] Witness: on such a host, `scrollWidth === clientWidth` after boot and after a pin → rail → pin-back cycle; the shell's x stays at the host's left edge.
- [ ] The Workstation and Demo-A keep their current overlay geometry (no visual change to previews; drop regions still resolve host-locally).
- [ ] Consumer duplicates of the rule are removed or annotated as overrides.

## Out of Scope

- Programmatic `focus()` calls without `preventScroll` during a staged re-projection (a separate hygiene item; harmless once the host cannot stay scrolled).
- The reconciler's behaviour when one of its own updates rejects mid-transaction (filed separately).

## Avoided Traps

- `overflow-x: clip` on the host would also stop the scroll but hides the cause: the preview would still be an in-flow fit item consuming a full host width in the flex row.
- Positioning the preview from `DragAffordances` at runtime (inline style) puts a layout constant on a per-drag code path; the stylesheet is the owner.

## Related

- Epic #13158 (docking polish).
- #18138 — the same ownership pattern: a rule the engine's reveal needs, living in consumer stylesheets.
- Prior instance of the same omission on the Workstation: the July 2026 finding that its overlays were drawn a header height too high; repaired in app SCSS rather than in the engine sheet.
